![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068356/assets/99504eaa41497c5be9baa7c860c97ab5ba5c858609e47ad347f24ec9b8ffc940.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
after.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(3,6,8)$ and $Q(-2,-5,4).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ -11t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-5t \\ 6-11t \\ 8-4t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-5t \\ y=6-11t \\ z=8-4t\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ -11t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-5t \\ 6-11t \\ 8-4t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-5t \\ y=6-11t \\ z=8-4t\end{aligned}

$$

$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+4t \\ 4-t \\ -2+2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+4t \\ y=4-t \\ z=-2+2t\end{aligned}

content.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+4t \\ 4-t \\ -2+2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+4t \\ y=4-t \\ z=-2+2t\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{2}t+1 \\ y=5-\frac{1}{2}t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}t+1 \\ 5-\frac{1}{2}t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}t \\ -\frac{1}{2}t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(1,5,\frac{1}{3})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{2}t+1 \\ y=5-\frac{1}{2}t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}t+1 \\ 5-\frac{1}{2}t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}t \\ -\frac{1}{2}t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(1,5,\frac{1}{3})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ -t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-3t \\ 4-t \\ -2+3t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$
